messages:
Sam W: Heads-up — p95 for tiny streaming responses spiked after last runtime rollout, mostly for <=64 byte chunks. Numbers: p50 ~55ms, p95 jumped from ~90ms -> ~130ms in prod canary. Looks host-side (ingress proxy) not decode.
Priya R: Ugh, I saw that on dashboards this morning. Any tracing / flame?
Sam W: Quick flame/snippet from one repro host:
```
  30.2%  host-proxy    [.] writev
  15.8%  host-proxy    [.] sendmsg (MSG_MORE)
  12.4%  host-proxy    [.] __socket_flush
```
Also getting a bunch of small write syscalls; suspect we introduced more eager flushes in the token bundler sampler.
Jorge L: Which change specifically? the sampler flush-on-chunk vs flush-on-time?
Sam W: We changed sampler to flush immediately on chunk boundary for streaming to reduce latency for long responses. That helped long tails but for many short responses it causes too many small TCP writes (MSG_MORE/partial buffers).
Priya R: Could be Nagle / TCP_NODELAY interactions. Are we setting NODELAY?
Sam W: We do set TCP_NODELAY on egress sockets, and we also use `sendmsg(..., MSG_MORE)` in the proxy to try to batch trailing frames. But when chunk size <=1 token we end up calling write per token.
Jorge L: Quick hypothesis: small writes prevent kernel coalescing and cause syscall overhead + socket flush latency. Two options: 1) add a short batching window (eg 3-5ms) for small chunks; 2) switch to writev aggregation in the ingress path to reduce syscalls.
Priya R: Can we toggle MSG_MORE usage? Maybe only use MSG_MORE when we know more than X bytes are queued.
Sam W: Agreed. Did a canary flip locally: disabled eager-flush on <64B chunks and aggregated up to 4 tokens or 5ms. Results on the same host: p95 went from 130ms -> 98ms, p50 unchanged.
Jorge L: Nice. Any impact on memory or KV cache behavior? If we hold for 5ms we might increase outstanding requests and affect KV cache hit ordering.
Sam W: Measured KV cache accesses — no extra misses. The KV cache is on-model-side; this is ingress timing only. However batching changes the request interleaving into the runtime which could change kernel selection heuristics if request shapes cluster differently.
Priya R: Good to note. Also check gRPC vs HTTP pathways — are both affected?
Sam W: Both show similar symptom on hosts using socket transport. HTTP/1 keepalives show slightly worse than HTTP/2 due to framing overhead. gRPC (HTTP/2) benefits from head-of-line multiplexing but still suffers syscall cost.
Jorge L: For short-term, let's:
- revert sampler to aggregate small tokens (sampler patch) on canary
- add socket-level writev fallback path to coalesce iovecs
- add perf test that sends 1-token responses at 2000rps to measure p95
Priya R: I'll open a tiny PR for sampler revert + test. Sam can you post the perf script?
Sam W: Perf repro (simple python async client):
```
import asyncio, grpc
async def spam():
  for _ in range(2000):
    await stub.Stream(...)  # server returns 1-token
```
Run for 30s and collect p95.
infra-bot: deploy v1.4.8 -> canary completed (hosts: runtime-canary-4) :white_check_mark:
Priya R: PR created: link: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/2345 (sampler: add 5ms/4-token aggregation fallback).
Jorge L: After canary flip, perf looks good. p95 dropped ~25-30ms on aggregate. Need to monitor for regressions in long-tail for long responses.
Sam W: Action items:
- Priya: land sampler revert + unit/perf tests (ETA today)
- Jorge: prototype writev aggregation path in ingress (ETA tom)
- Sam: run longer 4h canary and check model-level kernel-selection signals (so we don't flip heuristics unexpectedly).
Priya R: noted. Will also add a metric for "small-write-rate" (writes <128B) per host.
Sam W: Thanks — this was noisy in SLO slack earlier. Will update once canary 4h run is clean. :rocket:
